subject: Marketplace commission VAT routing & reverse-charge for MapleMart
messages:
From: Simon Keller <simon.keller@maplemart.co.uk>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: TaxOps <tax@maplemart.co.uk>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: VAT on marketplace commission — reverse-charge possible?

Hi Ben,

Quick question on behalf of our finance team — MapleMart runs a marketplace where we charge a 10% take rate on seller transactions. Many of the sellers are EU-registered B2B entities. We received Redwood's Q4 invoice (attached stub) that lists full commission amounts with VAT applied. Our TaxOps team would prefer to apply reverse-charge where the seller is VAT-registered to avoid double charging.

Can Redwood:
- Confirm whether you can issue your commission invoices to MapleMart net of VAT when we supply validated VAT IDs for the underlying sellers (so reverse-charge is applied by the seller)?
- Outline the evidence you need to validate seller VAT IDs (e.g., VIES check screenshot, VAT cert).
- Describe any invoice split or accounting changes we should expect on Redwood's side (do you issue a single aggregated invoice vs per-seller lines?).

Attaching current invoice and our VAT registration to help speed this along. Appreciate a short note and next steps.

Thanks,
Simon
Head of Finance, MapleMart

Attachments: MapleMart_Q4-2025-invoice.pdf (stub), MapleMart_VAT-registration-GB123456789.pdf (stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Simon Keller <simon.keller@maplemart.co.uk>
Cc: TaxOps <tax@maplemart.co.uk>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: VAT on marketplace commission — reverse-charge possible?

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Short answer: yes, in many EU cases we can support reverse-charge treatment, but it depends on how the contractual flow is set up and the evidence you can provide for each seller. Below is what we need and the expected billing behaviour.

What we need from you for each seller to consider reverse-charge on our commission:
- Seller legal name and VAT ID (exactly as registered)
- A VIES validation screenshot or the VIES query result (timestamped) showing the VAT ID is active
- Evidence that the seller is the VAT-registered party for the underlying sale (marketplace terms or reseller agreement)

How Redwood would handle invoices:
- If MapleMart wants Redwood to net VAT for commission lines, we can:
  1) Issue a single consolidated monthly invoice to MapleMart with commission lines shown net of VAT and a note that reverse-charge applies (per seller).
  2) Alternatively, issue per-seller sub-lines on the consolidated invoice if you provide a CSV mapping (seller_id, VAT ID, transaction total, commission amount).

Operational notes:
- We will run VIES checks on the provided IDs. If an ID fails validation, VAT will be applied until evidence is provided.
- For bookkeeping, our AP code will tag reverse-charge lines and include references to the provided VIES queries.
- The timeline for modifying existing invoices (e.g., reissuing Q4) requires review by Finance and may take 5–7 business days after we receive the validated CSV.

I'll loop in our billing team to confirm the CSV template. If agreeable, please share a sample CSV for 10 sellers and we'll run validation as a proof-of-concept.

Best,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Ben/Aditya — quick internal note on accounting and risk:

- We can support the consolidated invoice with per-seller sub-lines. Aditya, finance will need the CSV to include these minimal columns: seller_id, seller_name, seller_vat_id, transaction_gross, commission_amount, invoice_date, country_of_supply.
- We must capture a VIES query result for each seller (timestamp + raw response) and store it with the invoice for audit (EU tax authorities will ask). A screenshot is acceptable for now but an exported CSV from VIES or API query log is preferred.
- If MapleMart requests retroactive changes for Q4, we should only reissue if we can validate VAT IDs for the period (i.e., IDs were active at transaction time).
- Risk: if we accept MapleMart's mapping but a seller later cannot support their VAT registration, Redwood could be on the hook for VAT. We should include a clause in our marketplace billing that shifts final VAT responsibility to MapleMart for seller-level compliance; legal to advise.

I can review a small POC sample (10 sellers) once Aditya confirms CSV template and storage approach.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Billing & Treasury

Subject: Re: VAT on marketplace commission — reverse-charge possible?

Thanks — I've drafted the CSV template and a quick validation runbook. Key points: 

1) CSV template columns: seller_id, seller_name, seller_vat_id, vIES_query_datetime_utc, vIES_status, transaction_total_gross, commission_amount_gross, commission_amount_net, country_of_supply, maple_order_id

2) Validation runbook:
- Step A: Run VIES lookup via EU VIES API; store raw API response (JSON) and a short human-readable extraction (valid/invalid + name match).
- Step B: For UK VAT IDs (GB*), run an additional check against HMRC if VIES has issues post-Brexit.
- Step C: If status==valid, set commission_amount_net = commission_amount_gross and tag line as reverse-charge; else commission_amount_net = commission_amount_gross + VAT at seller country rate.

3) Implementation: Billing system can accept the CSV via a secure SFTP upload or via a signed upload link (we should provide both).

I attached a sample CSV (stub) and the runbook (stub). I'll drop the real template in the secure link if Ben wants to share with MapleMart.

-Aditya
Billing Systems Engineer

Simon — thanks for your patience. Per the thread above, we can run a POC to validate and apply reverse-charge to commission lines for MapleMart. Proposed next steps: 

1) MapleMart to provide a CSV with up to 50 seller rows (use Aditya's template). Please include a VIES export where possible.
2) Redwood runs validation and returns a report showing which seller lines passed/failed with recommended invoice treatment.
3) If results look good, Redwood will produce a consolidated invoice with per-seller sub-lines net of VAT where reverse-charge applies, and a short annex describing the evidence stored.

For Q4 adjustments: we will only reissue Q4 invoices for seller lines where the seller VAT ID validates as active at the time of the transaction. If you want retroactive reissue, add a column historical_vies_datetime and we'll check.

I've attached the sample CSV and runbook for convenience (stubs). If MapleMart is happy, reply with the preferred secure upload method (SFTP or signed upload link) and we'll provision credentials.

Ben
